security_spec.violation_condition: When XiangShan RTL implements Zvknhb (vsha2 at SEW=32 and SEW=64) but fails to also decode and execute the Zvknha subset (vsha2 at SEW=32 only), e.g., the instruction decoder gates SEW=32 vsha2 instructions solely on the Zvknha CSR enable bit without also enabling them when the Zvknhb CSR enable bit is set, or the ISA discovery CSR reports Zvknhb=1 but Zvknha=0
security_spec.summary: Zvknhb-implies-Zvknha: if XiangShan decoder gates SEW=32 vsha2 instructions exclusively on the Zvknha enable signal without also enabling them when Zvknhb is set, software on a Zvknhb-only-configured core will encounter illegal-instruction traps on valid SEW=32 SHA-2 operations, causing function loss

findings.finding: Neither Zvknhb nor Zvknha appears in the ISAExtensions list. The vulnerability condition (isZvknhb && !isZvknha) cannot occur because neither extension string is present. Scalar equivalents (zkn, zknd, zkne, zknh) are present at line 303, but their vector counterparts are absent. The list is a flat Seq with no subset/family group enforcement, so if Zvknhb were added in the future, nothing would enforce the spec requirement that it implies Zvknha.

No Zvknhb, Zvknha, or Zvknh BitPat object exists. Only Zvbb (lines 5-22) and Zimop (lines 24-27) are defined. The vsha2{ms, c.vv, c.vx, cl.vv, cl.vx} instructions have no encoding definitions anywhere in the codebase and are unconditionally treated as reserved/illegal. Since no decode entries exist, the vulnerability pattern (Zvknhb decode without Zvknha decode) cannot manifest.

The vector decode module only imports Zvbb._ (line 14). No import for Zvknhb/Zvknha/Zvknh BitPat objects exists because none are defined. The decode table (vset ++ opivv ++ ...) contains no entries for vsha2 instructions. All vsha2 opcodes will fall through to the default illegal-instruction path regardless of configuration.
findings.snippet:
import xiangshan.backend.decode.Zvbb._
// No Zvknhb, Zvknha import — none exists

findings.finding: VSew.isReserved treats all b1?? patterns as reserved encoding. This is extension-agnostic with no mechanism to conditionally reserve SEW=64 based on whether Zvknha (SEW=32 only) or Zvknhb (SEW=32 or 64) is enabled. However, since neither extension is implemented, this is latent infrastructure gap, not an active vulnerability.

spec_citations.excerpt:
zvknha: SEW is any value other than 32
zvknhb: SEW is any value other than 32 or 64

findings.finding: The BKU (Bit-manipulation/Crypto Unit) FuConfig only accepts IntData() source data and writes only the integer register file (writeIntRf=true, writeVecRf=false). It contains the SHA-256/SHA-512 round function datapath (sha256sum0/1, sha256sig0/1, sha512sum0/1, sha512sig0/1) needed by vsha2, but there is no vector register file interface. Vector vsha2 instructions would need either a new vector-to-BKU interface or a dedicated vector crypto execution unit.

The ISAExtensions list is a flat Seq[String] with no subset/family group enforcement. If future development adds Zvknhb to this list without also adding Zvknha, no compile-time or runtime check would prevent the violation. The security requirement is that Zvknhb implies Zvknha (spec norm:Zvknhb_impZvknha). The current infrastructure provides no guard against an implementer accidentally omitting Zvknha while declaring Zvknhb.
